# invariants-sidecar — full API reference

> Library-declared invariants as verified data. Two halves: the static-land core (dictionary completer + law/consistency property-test generator for tape-six-fast-check's `t.prop()`) and the sidecar-artifact toolchain (parser → compiler → three consumers: property tests, call-site guards, apodict oracle bridge). Zero runtime dependencies. ES modules; types and docs live in hand-written `.d.ts` sidecars.

Install:

npm install --save-dev invariants-sidecar tape-six tape-six-fast-check fast-check

Root export (`invariants-sidecar`) re-exports everything below except guards, which is subpath-only. Subpaths mirror `src/` (`invariants-sidecar/guards.js` etc.).

## src/static-land.js — dictionary completer

```ts
type StaticLandModule = Record<string, (...args: any[]) => any>;

interface Derivation {
  method: string; // method this row builds
  needs: string[]; // methods it builds from
  derive: (T: StaticLandModule) => (...args: any[]) => any;
}

interface ConsistencyObligation {
  method: string; // hand-provided derivable method
  needs: string[]; // base methods of the derivation it must agree with
  derivedFn: (...args: any[]) => any;
}

interface Completion {
  module: StaticLandModule; // input plus every derivable method, to fixpoint
  derived: Record<string, string[]>; // provenance: derived method -> base methods
  consistency: ConsistencyObligation[]; // one per hand-provided method per applicable derivation
}

const DERIVATIONS: Derivation[]; // the derivation lattice per the static-land spec

function complete(module: StaticLandModule): Completion;
```

`complete()` never overwrites a provided method. Consistency obligations implement static-land's consistency clause: a hand-provided derivable method owes agreement with every applicable derivation.

## src/laws.js — law records

```ts
// u/v/w — module values, a — plain value, f/g — plain unary functions,
// kf/kg — Kleisli functions (a -> T b)
type ArgKind = 'u' | 'v' | 'w' | 'a' | 'f' | 'g' | 'kf' | 'kg';

interface Law {
  typeclass: string;
  name: string;
  needs: string[]; // module methods the law reads; applies only when all exist
  args: ArgKind[];
  check: (T: StaticLandModule, eq: (x: unknown, y: unknown) => boolean) => (...values: any[]) => boolean;
}

const LAWS: Law[]; // Setoid, Semigroup, Monoid, Functor, Applicative, Chain, Monad

function lawsFor(T: StaticLandModule, typeclasses?: string[]): Law[];
```

## src/generate.js — property-test generator

```ts
interface ArbitraryLike {
  map(f: (value: any) => any): ArbitraryLike;
} // structurally a fast-check arbitrary; fast-check is NOT a dependency

interface GenerateOptions {
  arb: ArbitraryLike; // module values (u/v/w)
  arbA: ArbitraryLike; // plain values (a)
  arbFn: ArbitraryLike; // plain unary functions (f/g)
  arbK?: ArbitraryLike; // Kleisli functions; defaults to of-lifted arbFn
  arbUF?: ArbitraryLike; // lifted functions (T of a -> b) for ap-consistency; defaults to of-lifted arbFn
  equals?: (x: unknown, y: unknown) => boolean; // defaults to T.equals
  typeclasses?: string[]; // restrict generated law tests
}

interface LawTest {
  name: string;
  arbs: ArbitraryLike[];
  predicate: (...values: any[]) => boolean;
}

function makeLawTests(T: StaticLandModule, opts: GenerateOptions): LawTest[];
function makeConsistencyTests(T: StaticLandModule, opts: GenerateOptions): LawTest[];
function runLaws(t: {prop: Function}, tests: LawTest[]): Promise<void>;
```

`makeConsistencyTests` checks each hand-provided derivable method against every applicable derivation — a path routing through the corrupted method agrees by construction; the refuting paths come from the untainted base. `runLaws` needs tape-six-fast-check imported (side effect registers `t.prop`). The `of`-lifting defaults cannot reach values like a `Nothing`-shaped `T<fn>` — supply `arbK`/`arbUF` for those.

## src/parse.js — sidecar parser (inert)

```ts
interface Claim {
  kind: 'pre' | 'post' | 'effects' | 'complexity' | 'pattern' | 'hazard' | 'law';
  name: string;
  prose: string;
  qualifiers?: string;
  check?: {lang: string; source: string}; // inert source — compile explicitly
  trigger?: string; // pattern claims only
  replacement?: {lang: string; source: string};
  justification?: string;
  obligation?: string;
}

interface Sidecar {
  frontmatter: Record<string, string>; // package / binds / export
  name: string;
  description: string;
  claims: Claim[];
  implements?: string[]; // from a Laws section's "- implements:" line
}

function parseSidecar(text: string): Sidecar;
```

Parses the moonshot §6.5 artifact format — frontmatter, claim sections (Preconditions, Postconditions, Effects, Complexity, Patterns, Hazards, Laws) with backtick-named list items, and ```` ```js check kind:name ```` fenced blocks binding executable checks to claims by name. Loud, located errors on malformed input; never evaluates anything.

## src/compile.js — the trust step

```ts
function compileCheck(check: NonNullable<Claim['check']>): (...args: any[]) => any;
function compileChecks(sidecar: Sidecar): Record<string, (...args: any[]) => any>; // keys are `kind:name`
function lawTestsFromSidecar(sidecar: Sidecar, module: StaticLandModule, opts: GenerateOptions): LawTest[];
```

Compilation is the explicit trust step the parser refuses to take; it compiles but does not invoke. `lawTestsFromSidecar` bridges a Laws section to the static-land suite: `implements:` selects law sets, consistency obligations ride along, custom `law:` checks become extra properties called as `predicate(completedModule, ...values)`.

## src/guards.js — call-site guards (subpath-only)

```ts
interface GuardOptions {
  always?: boolean; // run predicates on every call, host or not; default honors "assumed, never checked at runtime"
}

function guardsFromSidecar(sidecar: Sidecar, opts?: GuardOptions): Record<string, (...args: any[]) => void>;
```

One guard per check-bearing `pre:` claim, keyed by claim name; each takes the check's own parameters and routes through tape-six-invariant's `check()` — a counted assertion when a tape-six run exercises the call site, the configured absent behavior otherwise. Importing `invariants-sidecar/guards.js` requires `tape-six-invariant`; the package core stays dependency-free. Pair `{always: true}` with `setAbsentBehavior(throwOnFail)` to pay for checks in production.

## src/oracle.js — apodict oracle bridge

```ts
interface AxiomTemplate {
  claim: string;
  name: string;
  source: string;
  atoms: Record<string, string>; // placeholder atoms
  formulas: unknown[]; // apodict §3 formulas
}

interface DeclareTemplate {
  claim: string;
  source: string;
  exports: Record<string, string[]>; // per-export flags (pure/total)
}

interface OracleInputs {
  axioms: AxiomTemplate[];
  declares: DeclareTemplate[];
}

function oracleInputsFromSidecar(sidecar: Sidecar): OracleInputs;
function instantiateAxioms(
  axioms: AxiomTemplate[],
  binding: Record<string, string>
): {formula: unknown; name: string; source: string}[];
function declareFromSidecar(declares: DeclareTemplate[], symbolExports: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string[]>;
```

Blessed claims become oracle inputs: a `law:` claim may carry a ```` ```json axiom ```` block, an `effects:` claim a ```` ```json flags ```` block. `instantiateAxioms` renames placeholder atoms to the consumer's query atoms (throws on an unbound placeholder); `name`/`source` flow into the law trail of any rewrite the axiom licenses. The bridge emits plain wire shapes and depends on nothing — the oracle (npm: `apodictum`) is not a dependency. Measured behavior: the oracle refuses a law-licensed rewrite until the sidecar also vouches `total` for the erased read.

## Notes

- All exports are named; there are no default exports.
- `exports` map: `.` -> `./index.js`, `./*` -> `./src/*` — subpath imports use the `.js` suffix.
- Docs: https://github.com/uhop/invariants-sidecar#readme
